_note: Real-style messages for the daily round. Each is a typical safe message: it asks for nothing, has no link to tap, and names no real company. 'why' explains the safe pattern in plain words.

items.body: Your sign-in code is 482913. It expires in 10 minutes. Never share this code with anyone.
items.why: You asked for this code. It has no link and tells you not to share it. Only type it into the app you just opened yourself.

items.body: Your prescription is ready for pickup at the store you chose. Reply STOP to end texts.
items.why: It asks for nothing. No link, no payment, no personal details. If you're unsure, call the store using a number you already have.

items.body: Reminder: you have a cleaning on Tuesday at 2:30 PM. Call the office if you need to change it.
items.why: It points you to the office you already know. It doesn't ask you to tap, pay, or confirm details.

items.body: Did you make a purchase of $42.10 today? If not, call the number on the back of your card.
items.why: It sends you to the number on your own card, not a number or link in the text. That's the safe way to check.

items.body: School is closed tomorrow because of snow. Watch the district website for updates.
items.why: It shares news and asks for nothing. You can check it yourself on a site you already know.

items.body: Running 10 min late, save me a seat!
items.why: A known contact, a normal message, no link, no request for money or codes.
